1	# TRUST_ASSUMPTIONS.md
2	
3	What the Verity port of the PQSigner smart-wallet contracts **does and
4	does not** verify. Matches Verity's own convention
5	([`lfglabs-dev/verity/TRUST_ASSUMPTIONS.md`](https://github.com/lfglabs-dev/verity/blob/main/TRUST_ASSUMPTIONS.md)).
6	
7	A default `lake build` compiles only the eight pure-Lean **Part B** modules.
8	It does **not** build `Theorems.lean` or establish any Part A wallet obligation.
9	Part A imports APIs absent from the pinned Verity release and remains unverified.
10	
11	`make verify-verity-census` freshly compiles all eight Part B modules with pinned
12	Lean 4.22.0 and inventories their exported declarations (including private and
13	generated declarations). It checks every declaration's transitive axiom closure,
14	not just theorem names or source keywords. Before the census, a separate
15	lean4checker kernel replay validates all 208 safe, non-partial Part B constants
16	against a separate environment imported from the pinned Lean distribution.
17	Constructors/recursors are compared with kernel-generated metadata. The five
18	existing partial compiler helpers are inventoried but excluded from replay;
19	unsafe project declarations are rejected. Ordinary `.olean` imports alone do
20	not recheck declarations added with kernel checking disabled.
21	
22	Each module's original private declaration data is checked before using the
23	merged environment: duplicate project names and stdlib redeclarations fail, and
24	the merged constants must equal that per-module union. This prevents a theorem
25	from silently subsuming an axiom declared in a sibling module.
26	
27	The checked baseline contains 15
28	environment axioms, of which two are project axioms, and one admitted Part B
29	helper: `PQSigner.Verifier.Merkle.yul_swap_selector_in_known_set`. Its name,
30	statement and admitted body are pinned; new dependents cannot inherit that
31	exception. A proof discharging the same statement is allowed.
32	
33	The five unbuildable Part A sources are instead pinned byte-for-byte. Their
34	11 source holes and CREATE2 axiom are **uncompiled, unverified obligations**.
35	Changing that quarantine or any census allowance requires an explicit reviewed
36	baseline change. The raw per-file hole count remains an additional backstop.
37	
38	The installed pinned Lean compiler, standard library, Python gate and reviewed
39	baseline are trusted. The gate does not sandbox compiler-time Lean IO or provide
40	a host filesystem isolation boundary. Toolchain/artifact custody during such IO
41	is part of the deferred build-assurance review, not established by this census. This is an exported-environment census, not an independent
42	kernel implementation, audit of transient anonymous examples, or proof of
43	Rust/Yul/Solidity equivalence. Lake caches and Part A cannot supply proof evidence
44	to this gate. See `assurance_inventory.json` for exact identities and hashes.
45	
46	## Part A intended obligations — not verified
47	
48	| Theorem | Statement | Implies CLAUDE.md invariant |
49	|---------|-----------|------------------------------|
50	| #1, #2, #3 | All three counter writers are monotonic and bounded by their caps. | #7 (per-chain caps monotonic) |
51	| #4 | `_removeOwnerAtIndex(0, _)` always reverts. | #6 (bootstrap immutable) — part 1 |
52	| #5 | No reachable trace overwrites `ownerAtIndex[0]` after construction. | #6 (bootstrap immutable) — part 2 |
53	| #6 | N-mask layout is enforced for every owner add. | (no CLAUDE.md mapping; defence-in-depth) |
54	| #7 | Factory salt has zero data dependence on `chainId`. | #6 (same address every chain) |
55	| #8 | `createAccount` is idempotent given identical args. | (no CLAUDE.md mapping; safety) |
56	| #9 | Distinct `chainId` ⇒ distinct squat-defence digest. | Squat-defence cross-chain |
57	| #10 | `ownerIndex == 0` dispatch only bumps `bootstrapUses`, only allows `addOwnerBytes`. | Dispatch correctness |
58	| #11 | `ownerIndex ≥ 1` dispatch never bumps `bootstrapUses`. | Dispatch correctness |
59	| #12 | EIP-1271 rejects `ownerIndex == 0`. | Bootstrap key never EIP-1271-signs |
60	| #13 | Global combined-cap invariant. | #7 (combined invariant) |
61	
62	## What is NOT verified (trusted axioms)
63	
64	> **Source axiom census (issue #673):** the tree declares exactly
65	> **3 `axiom`s** — `sha256_size` + `sha256_deterministic`
66	> (`PQSigner/Verifier/Hash.lean:40,47`; item 2 below) and
67	> **`predict_matches_create`** (`PQSigner/PQSmartWalletFactory.lean:65`;
68	> item 4 below — a content-bearing CREATE2 address-prediction claim, not
69	> merely a call-shape bridge). Only the Hash pair is elaborated by the Part B
70	> gate; the factory axiom is covered by the unverified Part A source quarantine.
71	
72	1. **`SPHINCsC10Asm.sol` correctness.** Modelled as opaque oracle
73	   `c10Verify : ByteVec → ByteVec → ByteVec → ByteVec → Bool`. We
74	   assume:
75	   - Deterministic in its inputs.
76	   - May revert (caller wraps in `try/catch`).
77	   - No observable side effect on our ERC-7201 namespace.
78	
79	   The verifier itself implements FIPS 205-aligned SPHINCS+C10 in
80	   hand-tuned Yul. Lifting this to a Lean theorem is the subject of
81	   `docs/archive/handoff-verity-c10-verifier.md`.
82	
83	2. **SHA-256 / Keccak-256 precompile correctness.** Both are
84	   axiomatised as the spec hash functions. Theorem #9
85	   (`addSlot0Digest_binds_chain_id`) relies on SHA-256
86	   collision-resistance — that is an assumption on the function, not
87	   a Lean-provable fact.
88	
89	3. **`solc 0.8.33` Yul → EVM bytecode correctness.** Verity's
90	   in-Lean compilation proof terminates at Yul; the Yul → bytecode
91	   lowering is `solc`. Pinning the version (matching Verity's own
92	   pin) is our only mitigation. Verity itself acknowledges this in
93	   its TRUST_ASSUMPTIONS.md.
94	
95	4. **Solady `LibClone` (`createDeterministicERC1967`,
96	   `predictDeterministicAddressERC1967`).** Axiomatised by:
97	
98	   ```lean
99	   axiom predict_matches_create :
100	     ∀ impl salt factory value,
101	       (createDeterministicERC1967 value impl salt factory).fst =
102	         predictDeterministicAddressERC1967 impl salt factory
103	   ```
104	
105	   The deeper claim — that the resulting address equals
106	   `CREATE2(factory, salt, ERC1967_INIT_CODE_HASH(impl))` — is a
107	   property of Solady's lib + the EVM CREATE2 opcode + `keccak256`.
108	   Out of scope.
109	
110	5. **EIP-1967 proxy `delegatecall` semantics.** All wallets are
111	   ~55-byte proxies that `DELEGATECALL` to the impl. We reason about
112	   the impl directly; the proxy is opaque and assumed semantics-
113	   preserving (this is a property of `DELEGATECALL` + EIP-1967, not
114	   our code).
115	
116	6. **EntryPoint v0.6 invariants.** The caller of `validateUserOp` is
117	   the EntryPoint singleton. We axiomatise that it follows ERC-4337
118	   v0.6 — specifically that it never calls `validateUserOp` with
119	   stale `missingAccountFunds` or skips the post-call settlement.
120	   Out of scope; trusted per the ERC-4337 spec.
121	
122	7. **Firmware-side wire format from CLAUDE.md §"Unified sign
123	   input".** The SHA-256 preimage that the firmware signs is *input*
124	   to our spec (via the opaque `sphincsDigest` function), not
125	   verified by it. If the firmware's `cmd_sign_userop.rs` builds the
126	   wrong preimage, the sigs it produces will be rejected on-chain —
127	   fail-safe, but the bug is not caught here.
128	
129	8. **`block.chainid` truthfulness.** The "same 24 words → same
130	   address on every chain" claim holds within a single canonical
131	   history per chain. An L2 reorg that retroactively reassigns its
132	   chain ID is out of scope (and would be a far larger problem than
133	   our wallet).
134	
135	9. **Gas griefing / OOG.** Verity does not reason about gas. The C10
136	   verify burns 1.7–4M gas; an attacker who supplies a malformed
137	   UserOp that triggers an OOG before the counter bump could leave
138	   storage in a stuck-pending state. Mitigation lives at the
139	   EntryPoint level (bundler gas estimation) and at the firmware
140	   level (slot-cache invalidation on OOG), not in this Lean proof.
141	
142	10. **`bumpBootstrapUses` is never called outside `validateUserOp`.**
143	    The chain of custody from "external entry point" to "counter
144	    bump" is part of theorem #10. If a future PR exposes
145	    `_bumpBootstrapUses` as a public function (or adds a new public
146	    entry point that calls it), theorem #10's premise no longer
147	    holds — but Lean would not catch it, because the new entry point
148	    is a new theorem obligation. **Code review remains responsible
149	    for noticing new public writers.**
150	
151	## Recovering trust when an axiom fails
152	
153	Each axiom corresponds to a specific failure mode:
154	
155	| Axiom failure | What breaks | Mitigation |
156	|---------------|-------------|------------|
157	| C10 verifier accepts a forged sig | Funds drainable from any slot | Part B handoff (Verity port of `SPHINCsC10Asm.sol`) |
158	| `keccak256` collision found | EIP-712 / CREATE2 collisions across the ecosystem | Industry-wide problem; out of scope |
159	| `sha256` collision found | Squat-defence digest reuse across chains | Industry-wide; out of scope. The combined-cap invariant still holds. |
160	| `solc 0.8.33` codegen bug | Verified Yul → buggy EVM bytecode | Differential test against the existing Solidity build catches behavioural divergence on test vectors |
161	| Solady `LibClone` deploys at wrong address | CREATE2 prediction differs from actual deploy | Solady is audited; if their pin moves, re-validate |
162	| EntryPoint v0.6 violates ERC-4337 | UserOp settlement breaks | Industry-wide; out of scope |
163	| Firmware builds wrong `sphincsDigest` preimage | Sigs rejected on-chain (fail-safe) | Firmware-side test in `secure/src/nsc/cmd_sign_userop.rs` |
164	
165	## Diff against `lfglabs-dev/verity/TRUST_ASSUMPTIONS.md`
166	
167	Verity's own list:
168	- Lean kernel correctness (trusted)
169	- `solc` Yul-to-bytecode correctness (trusted)
170	- `lake` build reproducibility (trusted)
171	
172	Our additions:
173	- C10 verifier (opaque oracle — the big one)
174	- Solady `LibClone` (axiomatised)
175	- EntryPoint v0.6 (axiomatised)
176	- Firmware-side wire format (input to spec)
177	
178	Our list inherits Verity's; the union is what reviewers should look
179	at before declaring a deployment "verified".

50	def source_snapshot(directory: Path) -> dict[str, bytes]:
51	    """Account for every project Lean source; reject links and unlisted roots."""
52	    found = {}
53	    if directory.is_symlink():
54	        raise ValueError("symlinked Verity directory")
55	    def error(exc):
56	        raise exc
57	    for parent, dirs, names in os.walk(directory, onerror=error):
58	        # Lake outputs/packages are deliberately outside the compilation boundary.
59	        if Path(parent) == directory:
60	            dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d != ".lake"]
61	        for name in dirs + names:
62	            path = Path(parent) / name
63	            if path.is_symlink():
64	                raise ValueError(f"symlink in Verity source: {path}")
65	        for name in names:
66	            path = Path(parent) / name
67	            if path.suffix == ".lean":

85	        resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_CPU, (110, 110))

89	        result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=directory, env=env, stdout=output,
90	                                stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=120, check=False, preexec_fn=limits)
91	        size = output.tell()
92	        if size > 8 * 1024 * 1024:
93	            raise ValueError("Lean census output exceeds 8 MiB")

21	def sameConstant : ConstantInfo → ConstantInfo → Bool
22	  | .axiomInfo a, .axiomInfo b => a == b
23	  | .defnInfo a, .defnInfo b => a == b
24	  | .thmInfo a, .thmInfo b => a == b
25	  | .opaqueInfo a, .opaqueInfo b => a == b
26	  | .quotInfo a, .quotInfo b => a == b
27	  | .inductInfo a, .inductInfo b => a == b
28	  | .ctorInfo a, .ctorInfo b => a == b
29	  | .recInfo a, .recInfo b => a == b
30	  | _, _ => false

32	def main (args : List String) : IO Unit := do
33	  initSearchPath (← findSysroot)
34	  let trusted ← importModules #[{ module := `Lean }] {} 0 (loadExts := false)
35	  let env ← importModules (args.toArray.map fun s => { module := s.toName }) {} 0 (loadExts := false)
36	  -- finalizeImport retains each module's original private ModuleData even
37	  -- though its combined name map can subsume an axiom with a sibling theorem.
38	  -- Census this union first: no cross-module duplicate or stdlib redeclaration
39	  -- may disappear into the aggregate environment used for kernel replay.
40	  let mut own : Std.HashMap Name ConstantInfo := {}
41	  let mut origins : Std.HashMap Name String := {}
42	  for module in args do
43	    let some idx := env.getModuleIdx? module.toName |
44	      throw <| IO.userError s!"Missing census module {module}"
45	    let data := env.header.moduleData[idx.toNat]!
46	    unless data.constNames.size == data.constants.size do
47	      throw <| IO.userError s!"Malformed module declaration arrays: {module}"
48	    for name in data.constNames, info in data.constants do
49	      unless name == info.name do
50	        throw <| IO.userError s!"Mismatched module declaration name: {module}"
51	      if origins.contains name then
52	        throw <| IO.userError s!"Duplicate project declaration {name} in {origins[name]!} and {module}"
53	      if trusted.contains name then
54	        throw <| IO.userError s!"Project redeclares trusted declaration {name} in {module}"
55	      own := own.insert name info
56	      origins := origins.insert name module
57	  let mut candidate : Std.HashMap Name ConstantInfo := {}
58	  for (name, info) in env.constants.toList do
59	    if let some original := trusted.find? name then

11	/-!
12	# `Lean.Environment.replay`
13	
14	`replay env constantMap` will "replay" all the constants in `constantMap : HashMap Name ConstantInfo` into `env`,
15	sending each declaration to the kernel for checking.
16	
17	`replay` does not send constructors or recursors in `constantMap` to the kernel,
18	but rather checks that they are identical to constructors or recursors generated in the environment
19	after replaying any inductive definitions occurring in `constantMap`.
20	
21	`replay` can be used either as:
22	* a verifier for an `Environment`, by sending everything to the kernel, or
23	* a mechanism to safely transfer constants from one `Environment` to another.
24	
25	## Implementation notes
26	
27	This is a patched version of `Lean.Environment.Replay`, which is in the `lean4` repository
28	up to `v4.18.0`, but will be deprecated in `v4.19.0` and then removed. Once it it removed,
29	the prime on the `Replay'` namespace, the prime on `Lean.Environment.replay'`
30	should be removed here.
31	
32	-/
33	
34	namespace Lean.Environment
35	
36	namespace Replay'
37	
38	structure Context where
39	  newConstants : Std.HashMap Name ConstantInfo
40	
41	structure State where
42	  env : Kernel.Environment
43	  remaining : NameSet := {}
44	  pending : NameSet := {}
45	  postponedConstructors : NameSet := {}
46	  postponedRecursors : NameSet := {}
47	
48	abbrev M := ReaderT Context <| StateRefT State IO
49	
50	/-- Check if a `Name` still needs processing. If so, move it from `remaining` to `pending`. -/
51	def isTodo (name : Name) : M Bool := do
52	  let r := (← get).remaining
53	  if r.contains name then
54	    modify fun s => { s with remaining := s.remaining.erase name, pending := s.pending.insert name }
55	    return true
56	  else
57	    return false
58	
59	/-- Use the current `Environment` to throw a `Kernel.Exception`. -/
60	def throwKernelException (ex : Kernel.Exception) : M Unit := do
61	  throw <| .userError <| (← ex.toMessageData {} |>.toString)
62	
63	/-- Add a declaration, possibly throwing a `Kernel.Exception`. -/
64	def addDecl (d : Declaration) : M Unit := do
65	  match (← get).env.addDeclCore 0 d (cancelTk? := none) with
66	  | .ok env => modify fun s => { s with env := env }
67	  | .error ex => throwKernelException ex
68	
69	mutual
70	/--
71	Check if a `Name` still needs to be processed (i.e. is in `remaining`).
72	
73	If so, recursively replay any constants it refers to,
74	to ensure we add declarations in the right order.
75	
76	The construct the `Declaration` from its stored `ConstantInfo`,
77	and add it to the environment.
78	-/
79	partial def replayConstant (name : Name) : M Unit := do
80	  if ← isTodo name then
81	    let some ci := (← read).newConstants[name]? | unreachable!
82	    replayConstants ci.getUsedConstantsAsSet
83	    -- Check that this name is still pending: a mutual block may have taken care of it.
84	    if (← get).pending.contains name then
85	      match ci with
86	      | .defnInfo   info =>
87	        addDecl (Declaration.defnDecl   info)
88	      | .thmInfo    info =>
89	        addDecl (Declaration.thmDecl    info)
90	      | .axiomInfo  info =>
91	        addDecl (Declaration.axiomDecl  info)
92	      | .opaqueInfo info =>
93	        addDecl (Declaration.opaqueDecl info)
94	      | .inductInfo info =>
95	        let lparams := info.levelParams
96	        let nparams := info.numParams
97	        let all ← info.all.mapM fun n => do pure <| ((← read).newConstants[n]!)
98	        for o in all do
99	          modify fun s =>
100	            { s with remaining := s.remaining.erase o.name, pending := s.pending.erase o.name }
101	        let ctorInfo ← all.mapM fun ci => do
102	          pure (ci, ← ci.inductiveVal!.ctors.mapM fun n => do
103	            pure ((← read).newConstants[n]!))
104	        -- Make sure we are really finished with the constructors.
105	        for (_, ctors) in ctorInfo do
106	          for ctor in ctors do
107	            replayConstants ctor.getUsedConstantsAsSet
108	        let types : List InductiveType := ctorInfo.map fun ⟨ci, ctors⟩ =>
109	          { name := ci.name
110	            type := ci.type
111	            ctors := ctors.map fun ci => { name := ci.name, type := ci.type } }
112	        addDecl (Declaration.inductDecl lparams nparams types false)
113	      -- We postpone checking constructors,
114	      -- and at the end make sure they are identical
115	      -- to the constructors generated when we replay the inductives.
116	      | .ctorInfo info =>
117	        modify fun s => { s with postponedConstructors := s.postponedConstructors.insert info.name }
118	      -- Similarly we postpone checking recursors.
119	      | .recInfo info =>
120	        modify fun s => { s with postponedRecursors := s.postponedRecursors.insert info.name }
121	      | .quotInfo _ =>
122	        addDecl (Declaration.quotDecl)
123	      modify fun s => { s with pending := s.pending.erase name }
124	
125	/-- Replay a set of constants one at a time. -/
126	partial def replayConstants (names : NameSet) : M Unit := do
127	  for n in names do replayConstant n
128	
129	end
130	
131	/--
132	Check that all postponed constructors are identical to those generated
133	when we replayed the inductives.
134	-/
135	def checkPostponedConstructors : M Unit := do
136	  for ctor in (← get).postponedConstructors do
137	    match (← get).env.find? ctor, (← read).newConstants[ctor]? with
138	    | some (.ctorInfo info), some (.ctorInfo info') =>
139	      if ! (info == info') then throw <| IO.userError s!"Invalid constructor {ctor}"
140	    | _, _ => throw <| IO.userError s!"No such constructor {ctor}"
141	
142	/--
143	Check that all postponed recursors are identical to those generated
144	when we replayed the inductives.
145	-/
146	def checkPostponedRecursors : M Unit := do
147	  for ctor in (← get).postponedRecursors do
148	    match (← get).env.find? ctor, (← read).newConstants[ctor]? with
149	    | some (.recInfo info), some (.recInfo info') =>
150	      if ! (info == info') then throw <| IO.userError s!"Invalid recursor {ctor}"
151	    | _, _ => throw <| IO.userError s!"No such recursor {ctor}"
152	
153	end Replay'
154	
155	open Replay'
156	
157	/--
158	"Replay" some constants into an `Environment`, sending them to the kernel for checking.
159	
160	Throws a `IO.userError` if the kernel rejects a constant,
161	or if there are malformed recursors or constructors for inductive types.
162	-/
163	def replay' (newConstants : Std.HashMap Name ConstantInfo) (env : Environment) : IO Environment := do
164	  let mut remaining : NameSet := ∅
165	  for (n, ci) in newConstants.toList do
166	    -- We skip unsafe constants, and also partial constants.
167	    -- Later we may want to handle partial constants.
168	    if !ci.isUnsafe && !ci.isPartial then
169	      remaining := remaining.insert n
170	  let (_, s) ← StateRefT'.run (s := { env := env.toKernelEnv, remaining }) do
171	    ReaderT.run (r := { newConstants }) do
172	      for n in remaining do
173	        replayConstant n
174	      checkPostponedConstructors
175	      checkPostponedRecursors
176	  return .ofKernelEnv s.env
